patients.summary: Retired teacher with non-valvular atrial fibrillation on warfarin managed by the practice, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and hip and knee osteoarthritis. A heparin bridge for her 2025 right hip replacement caused HIT with a left femoral arterial thrombus; heparin prophylaxis after her January 2026 left knee replacement brought a DVT, a segmental PE and recurrent thrombocytopenia. Outside records arrive late or not at all.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

66 y/o retired elementary school teacher transferring care. Main reason for the switch is anticoagulation: has had AF for years, on warfarin with a goal INR of 2-3, and wants her INRs run and acted on in one place.

AF: no palpitations she notices, no lightheadedness, no exertional chest discomfort. Never had a stroke or bleed on warfarin. Rate controlled on metoprolol succinate.
HTN: home readings low 130s. On lisinopril.
Lipids: on atorvastatin for years, no muscle complaints.
Joints: both hips and both knees ache with standing and stairs, right hip the worst. Uses acetaminophen, avoids ibuprofen because of the warfarin. Walks with friends most mornings, slower than she used to.

PSH: cholecystectomy (laparoscopic) and cataract surgery both eyes, years ago.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg nightly, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, calcium carbonate/vitamin D 600 mg/400 IU twice daily, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: sulfa (rash).
FH: father had an MI at 72 and high blood pressure. Mother had AF and an ischemic stroke at 75. Sister had a DVT after a delivery. No bleeding disorders in the family.
SH: lives alone in Amherst. Quit cigarettes about 20 years ago, 20 pack-years. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. Drives, independent.

Exam: well, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed laparoscopic scars. Extremities without edema; hips with reduced internal rotation, right more than left, crepitus at both knees. Neuro grossly intact.

ECG: AF, rate controlled, no acute changes.

A/P
1. Non-valvular AF on warfarin. INR today, we will take over INR management; monthly checks to start. Discussed bleeding precautions and checking with us before any antibiotic.
2. HTN, controlled. Continue lisinopril.
3. Hyperlipidemia. Continue atorvastatin; lipids with yearly labs.
4. OA hips/knees. Acetaminophen as needed; keep walking.
5. Health maintenance: records requested from prior practice. Flu and COVID shots next month.

Return 3 months, INR in 4 weeks.

Orthopaedic Surgery - Joint Replacement Service
Date of visit: 06/27/2024
RE: Sandra Kendall, DOB 04/10/1957

Thank you for the referral. Ms. Kendall is a 67-year-old woman with right hip pain for several years, worse this past year, now limiting her walking and waking her at night.

PMH: atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, OA of hips and knees.
Medications: warfarin, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, atorvastatin, calcium/vitamin D, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: sulfa (rash).

Exam: antalgic gait. Right hip flexion to 95 degrees with internal rotation to 5 degrees, painful at end range. Left hip with mildly reduced rotation. Neurovascularly intact distally.

Imaging: AP pelvis and right hip radiographs today show advanced osteoarthritis of the right hip with joint space loss and marginal osteophytes. Milder degenerative change on the left.

Impression: end-stage right hip osteoarthritis.

Plan: we discussed total hip arthroplasty versus continued conservative care. She would like to wait and get through another year, and is thinking of next summer. Continue acetaminophen and activity as tolerated. She will call when ready and we will arrange pre-operative evaluation, including a plan for her anticoagulation.

Orthopaedic Surgery

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - Orthopedic Surgery
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/07/2025  Discharged: 07/17/2025
Service: Orthopaedic Surgery (Hospital Medicine and Vascular Surgery consulting)
Patient: Sandra Kendall, 68F

Allergies at discharge: HEPARIN (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia - all heparin products including LMWH and flushes). Sulfa (rash).

Principal procedure: Right total hip arthroplasty, 07/07/2025. Uncomplicated intraoperatively.

Discharge diagnoses:
1. Right hip osteoarthritis, s/p right THA
2. Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
3. Acute arterial thrombosis, left femoral artery
4. Atrial fibrillation on chronic warfarin
5. Hypertension; hyperlipidemia

Hospital course: Warfarin had been held from 07/01 with an enoxaparin bridge from 07/03, resumed after surgery. On post-operative day 3 (07/10) she reported new pain in the left foot. The foot was pale and cool with diminished dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses. Platelets had fallen from 240 K/uL on admission to 80 K/uL. PT and aPTT were normal. Arterial duplex showed thrombus in the left femoral artery. HIT was suspected; all heparin was stopped and an argatroban infusion begun. PF4/heparin antibody ELISA returned positive (OD 1.84). Vascular surgery evaluated and recommended anticoagulation without operative intervention. Foot pain and pallor resolved and pedal pulses were again palpable by 07/14. Warfarin was restarted at 5 mg once platelets recovered above 150 K, overlapped with argatroban until INR therapeutic.

At discharge: platelets 168 K/uL, INR 2.6. Hip incision clean, weight bearing as tolerated with walker. Left foot warm, pulses palpable.

Discharge medications: warfarin 5 mg nightly (INR goal 2-3), metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, calcium carbonate/vitamin D twice daily, acetaminophen as needed. Enoxaparin discontinued.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks for CBC and INR. Orthopaedics at 6 weeks. HEPARIN ALLERGY TO BE ADDED TO ALL RECORDS; avoid all heparin products lifelong.

Dictated by Hospital Medicine for Orthopaedic Surgery. Faxed 08/20/2025.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharged 7/17 after R THA 7/7. Contact made 7/18.

Per patient (summary not yet received; she forgot the packet): on post-op day 3 her left foot turned pale and painful, platelet count had dropped, a clot was found in the left femoral artery, and she was told it was heparin-induced thrombocytopenia from the enoxaparin. Treated with an IV non-heparin anticoagulant, no surgery on the leg. Back on warfarin 5 mg before discharge.

Today: hip sore but improving, walker in the house, cane outside. Home PT twice a week. Left foot normal - no pain, no color change, no numbness. No bleeding, no calf pain, no chest pain or dyspnea.

Exam: incision R lateral hip healing, staples out, no erythema. L foot warm, normal color, DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally. No calf tenderness. Irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. HIT with L femoral arterial thrombosis, July 2025 - foot recovered. Problem list updated. She must never receive heparin of any kind; told her to say so at every visit, ER and pharmacy. CBC today to confirm platelet recovery.
2. AF on warfarin - INR today, then weekly x2 given recent restart.
3. s/p R THA - PT, ortho follow-up at 6 weeks.
4. Records request to hospital for discharge summary.

PRE-OP EVAL - L TKA planned 1/8/2026 (outside orthopedics)

History notable for HIT with left femoral arterial thrombosis after an enoxaparin bridge for her R THA in July 2025 (PF4 antibody positive). Fully recovered.

No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations or edema. Walks 20-30 min on level ground, limited by the knee. Tolerated anesthesia in July.

Meds: warfarin 5 mg, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, calcium/D, acetaminophen prn.
ALLERGIES: HEPARIN - HIT (all heparins incl. enoxaparin and flushes). Sulfa - rash.

Exam: irregularly irregular, controlled. Lungs clear. No edema. R hip incision healed. L knee crepitus, mild varus.
ECG 6/2025 unchanged rhythm; not repeated.

Assessment: medically acceptable risk for L TKA.

Recommendations to surgical team:
1. NO HEPARIN PRODUCTS of any kind - prior HIT with thrombosis. No LMWH bridge. If anticoagulant prophylaxis is needed before INR is therapeutic, use a non-heparin agent.
2. Warfarin hold per surgeon; given the HIT history I would not bridge.
3. Continue metoprolol; hold lisinopril morning of surgery.

Faxed to orthopedic pre-admission testing with today's labs.

reports.conclusion: Acute deep vein thrombosis, left lower extremity.

reports.text: CT pulmonary angiogram. Adequate opacification of the pulmonary arteries. Filling defect in a segmental pulmonary artery branch consistent with acute pulmonary embolus. Main and lobar pulmonary arteries patent. Heart size normal, no RV dilatation. No pleural effusion or consolidation.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 01/15/2026, arrival 08:50
Patient: Sandra Kendall, 68F
Allergies: Heparin (HIT); sulfa (rash)

CC: L calf pain and swelling

HPI: 68F POD 7 from L total knee arthroplasty (01/08/2026, this hospital system's orthopaedic service), discharged home 01/11. Two days of progressive pain and swelling of the left calf. Has been giving herself subcutaneous heparin injections twice a day since surgery per discharge orders; warfarin restarted after surgery. History of HIT with arterial thrombosis 07/2025. AF on chronic warfarin.

Meds: warfarin 5 mg, heparin 5,000 units SC q12h, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, calcium carbonate/vitamin D, acetaminophen.

Triage vitals stable. Exam: L knee incision intact with expected swelling. Left calf erythematous, warm and tender. Distal pulses present.

Labs: Hgb 13.2 g/dL, WBC 7.8 x10^9/L, platelets 55 x10^9/L (150 before surgery). PT 12 s, aPTT 35 s. D-dimer elevated.
LE venous duplex: acute DVT, left leg.

ED course: heparin stopped; hematology contacted. At 11:40, sudden shortness of breath and chest pain. BP 130/85, HR 110, SpO2 92% on room air; supplemental oxygen given. CT pulmonary angiogram: segmental PE. HIT antibody sent. Argatroban infusion started per hematology.

Impression: 1. Acute left leg DVT. 2. Acute segmental pulmonary embolism. 3. Thrombocytopenia with heparin re-exposure in patient with prior HIT - suspected recurrent HIT.

Disposition: admitted to medical ICU, 14:30.

Record faxed to PCP 01/20/2026.

documents.body:
PATIENT DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS - scanned from patient's copy at PCP visit 01/27/2026

Name: Sandra Kendall
Admitted 01/15/2026 (ICU, then medical floor). Discharged 01/22/2026.
Reason for stay: blood clot in left leg and blood clot in the lung. Low platelets from heparin (HIT). HIT antibody test: POSITIVE.

ALLERGY: HEPARIN - never receive heparin in any form (shots, IV, line flushes, enoxaparin).

In the hospital you received argatroban (IV blood thinner) and your warfarin was restarted and overlapped.
At discharge: platelets 162, INR 2.3.

Your medicines: warfarin 5 mg every evening; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 20 mg daily; calcium + vitamin D twice daily; acetaminophen as needed. STOP heparin injections.

Follow up: primary care within 1 week for INR and blood count. Orthopaedics as scheduled.
Return to the ER for chest pain, trouble breathing, new leg swelling, or bleeding.

documents.body: ED record from 1/15 arrived by fax: DVT L leg and PE after knee replacement, low platelets, admitted to ICU. We had no notice of the admission. Called pt's cell, no answer, left VM. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Home From Hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm home since yesterday. Sorry I missed your call - I was in the hospital for a week. Clots in my leg and lung after the knee surgery, and my platelets dropped again because of heparin shots they sent me home with. I'm back on warfarin only. They said see you within a week. Sandra

documents.title: Home From Hospital - Reply
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sandra, I'm glad you're home. We have you Tuesday 1/27 at 10:00 with blood work. Please bring every paper they gave you. Go to the ER for chest pain, worse breathing or any bleeding.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharged 1/22. Interactive contact 1/23 via portal.

Course (ED record + her discharge instruction sheet; no discharge summary or knee surgery records received): L TKA 1/8, discharged 1/11 on warfarin plus SC heparin 5,000 units twice daily. On POD 7 to the ED with 2 days of L calf pain/swelling - DVT on duplex, platelets 55. While in the ED developed dyspnea and chest pain, CTPA segmental PE, ICU admission. HIT antibody positive. Argatroban, warfarin overlapped. Discharged on warfarin 5 mg with platelets 162 and INR 2.3.

Today: breathing back to normal, no chest pain. L calf still a bit swollen and tender but better each day. Knee stiff, doing PT exercises. No bleeding.

Exam: comfortable on room air. Irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear. L knee incision healing, no drainage. L calf mildly swollen, minimal tenderness, no erythema.

A/P:
1. Acute L leg DVT and segmental PE, provoked (surgery), on warfarin - she stays on warfarin indefinitely for AF regardless. INR today; weekly for a month.
2. HIT, recurrent with heparin re-exposure. Platelets today to confirm recovery. Allergy prominent on chart and bracelet.
3. s/p L TKA - PT, ortho f/u.
4. Records: front desk to request discharge summary, ICU records and knee surgery op note.
5. Follow up in 4 weeks.
